lead.headline: Coldcard Fourth Attack Wave Nets 389 BTC as Hardware Wallet Security Model Faces Systemic Test
lead.tldr: A suspected fourth wave of Coldcard breaches exposes persistent vulnerabilities in air-gapped hardware wallet security, while the SEC's selective pace on bitcoin derivatives and Saylor's resumed accumulation signal divergent institutional risk appetites.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today's brief tracks how a single hardware wallet's repeated compromise is forcing a reassessment of self-custody risk models just as institutional bitcoin exposure mechanisms face their own regulatory friction.

top_signals.title: Coldcard Likely 4th Attack Wave Sweeps Nearly 389 BTC: Galaxy
top_signals.summary: Galaxy's Alex Thorn has identified a suspected fourth wave of attacks targeting Coldcard users. The breach reportedly impacted 462 addresses, resulting in the loss of approximately 388.93 BTC.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The scale and repetition of Coldcard breaches—now four waves totaling hundreds of BTC—suggests the attack vector is replicable and not yet patched, making hardware wallet security a live underwriting concern for any treasury or custody architecture.

top_signals.title: SEC keeps Nasdaq bitcoin options on hold after granting CME review
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's decision to keep Nasdaq bitcoin options on hold after granting CME review indicates a deliberate sequencing of derivatives market structure that will advantage incumbent futures venues over spot optionality in the near term.

top_signals.title: Sen. Bernie Moreno says Rep. Max Miller shouldn’t serve in the House, calling former son-in-law a ‘danger to my daughter’ and granddaughter
top_signals.why_it_matters: Political infighting between crypto-aligned lawmakers introduces governance noise that could complicate legislative timelines for digital asset frameworks, even if it does not directly alter policy substance.

top_signals.title: Saylor hints at Strategy bitcoin buy after five-week pause as STRC rate stays at 12%: 'Bitcoin Drive engaged'
top_signals.why_it_matters: Saylor's resumed accumulation at a 12% STRC rate signals that Strategy's cost of capital remains tolerable for levered bitcoin exposure, maintaining a bid that underwrites price floors even if it concentrates market risk in one vehicle.

top_signals.title: As Trump balks again at escalating war, Iran smells ‘blood in the water’ and looks to exploit its newfound strategic advantage, experts say
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical hedging behavior in energy markets typically correlates with bitcoin volatility regimes, and any sustained Iran-Israel escalation would test whether current derivatives pricing adequately reflects tail risk.

Coldcard Likely 4th Attack Wave Sweeps Nearly 389 BTC: Galaxy

linkedin_post:
Four waves. 462 addresses. 389 BTC. The Coldcard numbers are accumulating faster than most firmware patches.

Galaxy's Alex Thorn has now identified what looks like a fourth coordinated attack on Coldcard users. The pattern is stubborn: air-gapped does not mean air-tight when the supply chain or user setup introduces compromise. We're watching this because self-custody hardware is supposed to be the trust-minimized endpoint. If that endpoint keeps bleeding, the entire custody stack gets repriced—treasuries, insurers, wallet vendors, the layer beneath the layer.

Elsewhere, Saylor's back at the table. Strategy's STRC rate holds at 12%, and he's buying again after five weeks. That bid is mechanical. It also concentrates. One entity's cost of capital becomes everyone's implied floor.

The SEC, meanwhile, is moving in its own tempo. CME gets review; Nasdaq options stay parked. The sequencing matters. Futures first, spot derivatives later, if at all. That's not neutrality. That's market structure by appointment.

What would change our read? A Coldcard firmware release that actually closes the vector, with third-party attestation. Until then, we assume the fifth wave is already in progress.
